name: MIT Chapel
description: A non-denominational chapel in the form of a brick cylinder rising 33 feet, encircled by a shallow moat and topped with an aluminum bell tower. Undulating interior walls of clinker brick surround a space lit by a domed skylight, the chapel's only window. The altarpiece is by Harry Bertoia, and the spire and bell tower by sculptor Theodore Roszak were added in 1956. It seats up to 140 people.
significance_text: Dedicated in May 1955 alongside Saarinen's Kresge Auditorium, the chapel grew out of a postwar institutional interest in reinforcing the humanities at MIT. Both buildings have since been acknowledged as architectural landmarks.

admission.notes: Open to the general public during visiting hours, Monday to Friday, 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM and 1:30 PM to 2:30 PM. The chapel is not available for viewing during a service. MIT's page does not mention an admission fee.
